Quantile Treatment Effect level τ\tau QTE(τ)=QY(1)(τ)−QY(0)(τ)QTE(\tau) = Q_{Y(1)}(\tau) - Q_{Y(0)}(\tau), QY(d)(τ)Q_{Y(d)}(\tau) τ\tau-th quantile potential outcome distribution treatment status dd. Mapping QTE(τ)QTE(\tau) across τ∈(0,1)\tau \(0,1) traces treatment shifts entire outcome distribution. title: Quantile Treatment Effects in R
text: treatment randomly assigned, unconfoundedness assumption (conditional independence potential outcomes given covariates) provides identification (Firpo 2007). use observational Lalonde data (lalonde.psid), combines treated group experiment comparison group PSID. unc_qte() supports three estimation methods: "ipw" — inverse probability weighting (propensity score re-weighting) "reg" — outcome regression (conditional quantile regression) "aipw" — augmented IPW (doubly robust; recommended)  estimates large negative, far experimental benchmark . QTE whole population, mostly PSID households much higher earnings program’s participants, covariates (leave earnings program) make two groups comparable (LaLonde 1986; Dehejia Wahba 1999).

Six difference--differences-type assumptions, restrict untreated outcomes change time; one, lou_qtt(), selection--observables assumption conditions lagged outcome. vignette states assumption shows minimal call. full applied workflow (aggregations, event studies, testing whether effect location shift, covariates), see vignette("staggered-adoption"). use mpdta throughout: balanced panel 500 US counties observed annually 2003–2007, lemp (log employment) outcome first.treat cohort variable (year first minimum wage increase; 0 = never treated). common call structure seven estimators : gt_type = "qtt", estimator returns QTT curve together ATT implied assumption, bootstrap draws. plot shows overall QTT curve uniform confidence band overall ATT horizontal line. estimators except cdf_did() built quantiles ranks designed continuous outcomes. discrete outcome, one large mass point (many zeros), quantile treatment effects usually point identified, estimators warn.

Intuition: expression QYt(0)|D=g(FYt−1(0)|D=g(y))Q_{Y_t(0)|D=g}(F_{Y_{t-1}(0)|D=g}(y)) takes pre-period value yy, finds quantile rank group gg’s pre-period distribution, returns post-period value rank within group gg’s distribution. assumption requires operation give result groups every yy. can thought nonlinear version parallel trends: parallel trends requires mean Y(0)Y(0) shift equally across groups, CiC requires entire distributional time-change . Athey Imbens (2006) derive model Y(0)=h(U,t)Y(0) = h(U, t) hh increasing unobservables UU whose distribution change time within group. Identification: assumption counterfactual quantile function QYt(0)|D=1(τ)=QYt|D=0(FYt−1|D=0(QYt−1|D=1(τ))).Q_{Y_t(0)|D=1}(\tau) = Q_{Y_t|D=0}\!\left(F_{Y_{t-1}|D=0}\!\left(Q_{Y_{t-1}|D=1}(\tau)\right)\right). text: Computes Quantile Treatment effects Treated (QTT) Average Treatment Effect Treated (ATT) using Mean Difference--Differences identification strategy. Handles two-period data staggered treatment adoption uniformly. Supports panel repeated cross sections data. Identification. MDiD assumes counterfactual distribution untreated potential outcomes location shift treated group's pre-treatment distribution. size shift mean \(\Delta = E[Y_{\text{post}}|D=0] - E[Y_{\text{pre}}|D=0]\), \(Q_{Y(0),\text{post}|D=1}(\tau) = Q_{Y,\text{pre}|D=1}(\tau) + \Delta\). stronger parallel trends means alone: additionally requires shape treated group's outcome distribution unchanged counterfactual. MDiD special case QDiD applies single mean shift rather rank-specific distributional shift. Covariate adjustment. xformula specified, scalar shift replaced unit-specific conditional mean shift \(\Delta(X_i) = E[Y_{\text{post}}|D=0,X_i] - E[Y_{\text{pre}}|D=0,X_i]\), estimated weighted OLS. counterfactual treated unit \(\) \(Y_{\text{pre},} + \Delta(X_i)\), unconditional counterfactual distribution empirical CDF values. law iterated expectations, consistently estimates \(F_{Y(0),\text{post}|D=1}\).

text: Computes panel QTT counterfactual outcome distribution single (g,t) cell using three-period copula-stability estimator Callaway Li (2019). Serves directly attgt_fun argument ptetools::pte. Panel data required groups. Three periods treated (pre2, pre1, post) two control (pre1, post).
